sources.entry: RClick - Add new functionality to the macOS Finder context menu. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/wflixu/RClick) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: RClick is a macOS app that adds custom actions (open with apps, copy path, delete, hide/unhide, AirDrop, new file templates, quick-access folders) to the Finder right-click context menu.
summary.what_it_does: RClick runs as a SwiftUI menu bar app paired with a FinderSync extension that injects custom items into Finder's context menu. Its listed features include opening files or folders with another installed app (with custom arguments and environment variables), copying full paths to the clipboard, deleting items directly without using the Trash, toggling file visibility, and sharing via AirDrop. It can also create new files from templates (.txt, .json, .md, .docx, .pptx, .xlsx, and Apple's .pages, .key, .numbers) and pin frequently used folders to the menu. The README also describes a declarative custom_menu.json for hierarchical submenus, separators, and custom titles and icons. Settings are stored with SwiftData in a shared App Group container, and the two processes communicate through DistributedNotificationCenter.
use_cases: add custom actions to the Finder right-click menu
open files with a different app from Finder
create new files from templates in Finder
delete files without sending them to the Trash
pin favorite folders to the context menu
how_to_run: Select the RClick scheme, then Product → Build (⌘B)
Enable the Finder extension in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Extensions → Added Extensions
notable: Dual-process design: a menu bar app plus a FinderSync extension injected into Finder
Declarative custom_menu.json for nested submenus, separators, and custom titles/icons; invalid files leave the existing menu unchanged
Localized in English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, and French, with system language auto-detected
Create-new-file templates include Apple iWork formats (.pages, .key, .numbers)
caveats: Requires macOS 15.6+ and Xcode 16.4+ to build from source
The Finder extension must be manually enabled in System Settings, and per-folder authorization is prompted for file operations
Accessibility permission is needed for certain automation features
